newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called up $2.50, Brent up 5/10 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called up $2.50, Brent up 5/10 cts.

text.p: IPE oil futures were called to open higher on Wednesday in sympathy with a U.S. rally based on bullish gasoline demand and stock data, brokers said.
Front month August gas oil was expected to start business about $2.50 a tonne stronger following its settlement on Tuesday at $162.75 a tonne.
August Brent crude futures were expected to open between five and 10 cents stronger. The contract settled on Tuesday at $18.39 a barrel.
Brokers said gas oil's impetus would come mainly from playing catch-up with Brent, which continued to rally strongly in London after gas oil's close on Tuesday.
But they said the upside was limited, with $165.50 likely to remain a stubborn resistance point. They noted the APIs showed a continuing bearish rise in U.S. distillate inventories.
"The APIs will help (NYMEX crude) and gasoline but heating could well tail off later. There's no reason for it to go crazy and we'll probably run out of steam again below $165.50," a broke said.
Brent is likely to reflect crude futures' additional overnight strength on ACCESS following a dramatic recovery late on Tuesday on the back of expectations of strong API gasoline figures.
The API data showed gasoline demand running up 3.6 percent on a four-week average year-on-year basis in the week to July 11.
In Singapore August Brent was at $18.45, up six cents.
NYMEX August crude trading on ACCESS, was last traded at $19.76 a barrel, up nine cents from New York, which rose 86 cents to $19.67.
But some brokers said the effect of gasoline strength was already fully in the market, noting Tuesday's sharp rise indicated API data was well flagged to many players ahead of publication.
They noted bearish news that Iraq will probably have to export around 1.5 million barrels per day to meet a target of $1 billion in revenue in the first quarter of the new oil-for-food programme.
That level of exports is double the amount of the first 180-day period.
But some brokers said support could come from any further news of production woes in Colombia caused by rebel attacks.
August gasoline rose 1.59 cents per gallon to 59.94 in New York and added a further 0.61 cents on ACCESS to last trade at 60.55.
